Tooltip_PC_IronCross:
First World War-era German Iron Cross; 2nd Class.
Awarded for an act of bravery.
Tooltip_PC_PanamaCanal:
This medal dates to the early 20th century and has an additional bar reading 'Two Years.'
They were awarded to the various laborers who worked on the Panama Canal.
Tooltip_PC_MedalBook:
A book which provides numerous descriptions and pictures of various medals and awards.
It can be used to identify said items.
Tooltip_PC_MysteryMedal:
A shiny medal of some sort, although you're not entirely sure what its origins are or what it necessarily is outside of that.
Maybe there's a way to determine what it is?
Tooltip_PCComicBookBox: A handy cardboard box designed primarily to keep comics in, although given it's just a big box you could probably cram just about anything in it.
Tooltip_PC_Ostfront:
A German medal from the Second World War, the reverse side has the years 1941 and 1942 on it.
It was awarded to soldiers who served during the invasion of the Soviet Union in the winter months.
Tooltip_PC_PurpleHeart:
An American medal which was given to soldiers who were either killed or wounded in the line of duty.
The reverse reads 'For Military Merit' and the soldier's name which has been lost to time.
Tooltip_PC_PurpleHeartOakLeaf:
An American medal which was given to soldiers who were either killed or wounded in the line of duty.
There is an additional oak leaf to denote an additional injury incurred at another time.
Tooltip_PC_VietnamService: An American medal awarded to participants in the Vietnam War.
Tooltip_PC_VietnamServiceStars:
An American medal awarded to participants in the Vietnam War.
There are two bronze stars on the ribbon which denote additional campaigns.
Tooltip_PC_KoreanService: An American medal awarded to participants in the Korean War.
Tooltip_PC_GayMedal: A fine medal made of silver which bears the inscription 'Turbo Gay' on the front.
Tooltip_PC_FemboyMedal: A very fine medal awarded for distinction to a femboy.
Tooltip_PC_MysteryMedalSilly: This is a rather peculiar medal, you can't exactly tell what it's supposed to indicate but it is most certainly not a normal medal.
Tooltip_PC_SouthwestAsiaService: An American medal awarded to participants in the Gulf War.
Tooltip_PC_NationalDefenseService:
An American medal awarded to participants in a variety of time periods.
These include the Korean War, Vietnam War, and the Gulf War.
Tooltip_PC_EquestriaGuard:
An award granted to Equestrian Royal Guards for serving Equestria for 5 years.
It has enameled versions of the two princesses alongside a central blue star.
Tooltip_PC_WW1Service:
An award given to American participants during World War One.
There is a clasp on the medal which reads 'France.'
Tooltip_PC_WW2Service: An award given to American participants during World War Two.
Tooltip_PC_GARMedal:
An award signifying membership to the Grand Army of the Republic.
The G.A.R. was an organization of American Civil War veterans for nearly 100 years.
Tooltip_PC_PrussianNapoleonic:
An award granted to Prussian soldiers during the Napoleonic Wars, specifically for the years 1813 and '14.
It was forged from captured cannon.
Tooltip_PC_BritishAfghanMedal:
A medal from the UK granted to soldiers who participated in the 2nd Afghan War, both to British and to Indian troops.
The bar reads ' Ali Musjid' indicating participation at Khyber Pass.
Tooltip_PC_BritishSouthAfricaMedal:
A medal awarded to participants, civilian or military, present during the 2nd Boer War.
The bars read 'Transvaal' and 'Cape Colony'.
Tooltip_PC_BritishWarMedal: This medal was granted to soldiers serving under the British Empire during the First World War.
Tooltip_PC_MysteryMedalRare:
Looking this medal over, even without any sort of experience, you can gather that it seems to be rare.
Perhaps it's the luster on the metal, or maybe the foreign wording.
Tooltip_PC_MedalOfHonor:
This is the highest decoration available in the United States and is issued to those who have performed an act of extreme valor.
This version appears to be the type for the Army.
Tooltip_PC_VictoriaCross:
The highest award granted to Britain's soldiers, including its various colonial units, for bravery.
These medals date all the way back to the mid-XIX'th century, during the Crimean War.
Tooltip_PC_EdensGateCross: There's a garden through the gate, where the father keeps us safe.
Tooltip_PC_OrderRedStar:
A Soviet award issued for a variety of reasons throughout the various countries within the USSR.
According to the book, the wording on this medal reads 'Workers of the world, unite.'
Tooltip_PC_BronzeStarMedal:
An American medal granted to individuals who performed some act of valor in a combat setting.
These have been awarded since the Second World War.
Tooltip_PC_BrodieHelmet:
First World War-era American helmet copied very closely to the British pattern helmets.
There is a huge variety of different designs and colors that have surfaced over the years, maybe you got one of the fancy ones?
Tooltip_PC_SovietPolarMedal:
Second World War-era Soviet medal awarded to the military and civilians.
Given out for assistance in defending the arctic regions of the USSR after 1944.
Tooltip_PC_WhiteLionOrder:
A rather valuable looking medal, it appears to have been awarded in rather limited numbers.
This is the highest order awarded in Czechoslovakia.
Tooltip_PC_ButterflyCan:
A Butterfly-Brand can of 'Boston Marrow Squash.'
This brand dates back to the late 19th century.
Tooltip_PC_UnknownCan:
An old tin can, the label is a bit scuffed up and whatever contents it once held have been missing for a long, long time.
There must be some way to find out some more info about it.
Tooltip_PC_CanBook:
A reference book providing many images of tin can labels from various time periods.
It can be used to identify said items.
Tooltip_PC_SkylineCan:
Skyline-Brand Apples, packed by the Colorado Packing Corporation in Cañon City, Colorado.
This can features a net weight on the label, and so would indicate it is from after 1906.
Tooltip_PC_RoyalGorgeCan:
Royal Gorge-Brand Black Cherries, packed by the Round Crest Companies in Cañon City, Colorado.
The Round Crest cannery would be operated by the state prison for a long while before being demolished in 1974.
Tooltip_PC_ButterBoyCan:
Butter Boy-Brand Popcorn, packed in Mattoon, Illinois by Ray G. Redding.
There are several labels on the can including one which reads 'Pop Corn is a real health food' and goes on to discuss a variety of dishes it can be made with.
Tooltip_PC_1916Stahlhelm:
A German helmet first introduced into service in 1916 during the Great War.
These helmets provided ample protection for troops, however could prove uncomfortable when in the prone position.
Tooltip_PC_AdrianHelmet:
A helmet originally developed by the French during the First World War and was the first mass-issue helmet in modern warfare.
The Adrian saw extensive use through multiple armies, spanning into the Interwar years.
Tooltip_PC_VZ32Helmet:
This helmet saw its first appearance in 1932, being developed by the newly-formed Czechoslovakian First Republic.
These helmets saw use through the interwar years, WWII, and even post-war use for fire departments and other civilian purposes.
Tooltip_PC_M35Stahlhelm:
An infamous helmet most notably depicted alongside jackbooted German troops of the Second World War.
Coming out in 1935, these helmets would be exported to other nations including China.
Tooltip_PC_M1Helmet:
Arguably one of the most famous helmet designs in the world, conceptualized by the United States.
These helmets were the mainstay of US soldiers during the Second World War and would go on to be issued to many, many nations during the Cold War.
Tooltip_PC_HeadwearBook:
A book which provides numerous descriptions and photos of military hats and helmets.
It can be used to identify said items.
Tooltip_PC_HatBox:
An old, beat up wooden box designed to hold hats.
You need to make use of the Military Headgear Guide to identify what's inside.
Tooltip_PC_Pickelhaube:
An old German helmet with a spike adorned on the top, the history of these helmets dates back to the 1840s.
These are later-pattern models from around the turn of the century.
Tooltip_PC_BelgicShako:
A Napoleonic-era British shako inspired from Portuguese shakos of the period, this pattern being instituted in 1812.
One reason these came about was due to the lackluster appearance of the earlier 'Stovepipe' pattern and was designed to be as flashy as other armies' headwear.
Tooltip_PC_CampaignHat:
An American campaign hat, the kind seen from the Indian Wars period into the 20th century.
Perhaps the most famous use of these hats was during the Spanish-American War and the Rough Riders.
Tooltip_PC_38MHelmet:
These helemts were produced by Hungary and are heavily inspired by the German M35 stahlhelm.
Hungary would export the helmets to various nations, perhaps the most famous being Finland.
Tooltip_PC_Furajka:
A Russian soft cap dating to around World War 1 and was the standard military hat of the period.
These are rare to find stateside and so probably came from an American soldier serving in Siberia or an immigrant veteran.
Tooltip_PC_AustrianKasket:
An old Austrian helmet from the Napoleonic Wars primarily constructed of leather.
It boasts a wool comb in black and yellow, the colors of the Austrian Empire.
Tooltip_PC_RuskiKasket:
An old Russian helmet which had its inception in 1844 and made famous during the Crimean War.
It is reported that Tsar Nicholas I created the design and was visited by Prince Charles, who liked the design so much he implemented it within Prussian ranks.
Tooltip_PC_M3Tactical:
The standard-issue helemt of the Federation's Mobile Infantry.
You are not rated to repair it.
Tooltip_PC_HardeeHat:
A famous American hat most prominently utilized during the American Civil War.
These originally began to be issued in 1858 and came with a variety of insignia to adorn them with.
Tooltip_PC_MeijiHat:
An old Japanese visor cap, the pattern instituted on the 19th year of Emperor Meiji's reign.
These hats saw service from the mid-1880s, through the Taisho period, and even into World War II.
Tooltip_PC_HatM43:
A German field hat, "Einheitsfeldmütze," introduced in 1943 during the Second World War.
These hats were heavily inspired by civilian ski hats and the old Austro-Hungarian caps of WWI.
Tooltip_PC_HatFeldkappe:
A First World War-era military hat worn by the K.u.K. introduced in the early 20th century.
These hats were worn by many of the ethnicities serviving in the Austro-Hungarian forces.
Tooltip_PC_MitreCap:
These caps were often utilized by European grenadiers during the 18th and 19th centuries, initially to have an easier time lighting grenade fuses.
The first appearance of these caps were for Catholic and Orthodox religious figures such as bishops, and the tradition continues today.
Tooltip_PC_JacketGermanM1907:
An Imperial German service uniform issued in 1910 to replace the earlier blue uniforms for field service.
These were the uniforms worn at the outbreak of the First World War before being replaced by simplified patterns.
Tooltip_PC_Boots1866Marching: Originally introduced into Prussian ranks in 1866, these marching boots would see service into the Great War.
Tooltip_PC_PantsGerman1907:
German field trousers introduced in 1907 to bring the army up to a more modern picture.
These trousers would see service throughout the First World War and most have a distinctive red flair on the side.
Tooltip_PC_ValiseGermanWWIKit:
A set of German WWI-era field kit, including two sets of cartridge pouches and a bread bag.
During the Great War, most German soldiers did not use proper y-straps and instead had to rely on their bread bag strap to hold their equipment up.
Tooltip_PC_JacketGermanM1896:
A jacket introduced to German units stationed in its overseas colonies in 1896.
The original 1896 patterns were in a sand-like color, however in 1897 a gray model was introduced to be worn in the home country.
Tooltip_PC_JacketGermanM1915:
A German blouse which began to be issued in 1915 as a simplified pattern due to wartime shortages.
These tunics proved to be better-suited to the conditions of trench warfare.
Tooltip_PC_ScriptC:
This item is used by the game for randomizing an item.
Under normal gameplay you should not be seeing this item, your game may be lagging or there is a mod conflict.
Tooltip_PC_Puttees:
A pair of wool puttees often worn by soldiers and civilians alike.
Puttees have been worn for millennia, but most famously during the First World War.
